\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ترازو} (tarāzū)}{ترازو (tarāzū)}]{\ur{ترازو} (tarāzū) — a pair of scales; a balance}

\label{lesson:UR-C425-tarazu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a packet, then the Urdu for to wrap.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ترازو}}
\textbf{\ur{ترازو}} — \emph{tarāzū} — \textquotedblleft{}a pair of scales; a balance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دکاندار} \ur{ترازو} \ur{پر} \ur{سیب} \ur{تولتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dukāndār tarāzū par seb toltā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper weighs apples on the scales.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ترازو}} (\emph{tarāzū}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{tarāzū}, \textquotedblleft{}a balance, scales\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarāzū}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarāzū}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dukāndār tarāzū par seb toltā hai.} — The shopkeeper weighs apples on the scales.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a packet, then the Urdu for to wrap, then say \emph{tarāzū} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ترازو} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A pair of scales; a balance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مفت} (muft)}{مفت (muft)}]{\ur{مفت} (muft) — free of charge}

\label{lesson:UR-C425-muft}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to wrap, then the Urdu for a pair of scales.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مفت}}
\textbf{\ur{مفت}} — \emph{muft} — \textquotedblleft{}free of charge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دو} \ur{پیکٹ} \ur{خریدیے،} \ur{ایک} \ur{مفت} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{do paikaṭ kharīdiye, ek muft hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Buy two packets and you get one free.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مفت}} (\emph{muft}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{muft}, \textquotedblleft{}free, for nothing\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بقایا} (baqāyā)}{بقایا (baqāyā)}]{\ur{بقایا} (baqāyā) — money still owed; arrears}

\label{lesson:UR-C425-baqaya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a pair of scales, then the Urdu for free of charge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بقایا}}
\textbf{\ur{بقایا}} — \emph{baqāyā} — \textquotedblleft{}money still owed; arrears\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میں} \ur{نے} \ur{دکاندار} \ur{کا} \ur{بقایا} \ur{دیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṅ ne dukāndār kā baqāyā diyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I paid the shopkeeper what I still owed him.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بقایا}} (\emph{baqāyā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{baqāyā}, \textquotedblleft{}remainders, what is left over\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a pair of scales, then the Urdu for free of charge, then say \emph{baqāyā} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ریزگاری} (rezgārī)}{ریزگاری (rezgārī)}]{\ur{ریزگاری} (rezgārī) — loose change; coins}

\label{lesson:UR-C425-rezgari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for free of charge, then the Urdu for money still owed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ریزگاری}}
\textbf{\ur{ریزگاری}} — \emph{rezgārī} — \textquotedblleft{}loose change; coins\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دکاندار} \ur{کے} \ur{پاس} \ur{ریزگاری} \ur{نہیں} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dukāndār ke pās rezgārī nahīṅ thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper had no change.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ریزگاری}} (\emph{rezgārī}) is built on Persian \emph{reza}, \textquotedblleft{}a small piece\textquotedblright{}: it is usually traced to a Persian word for small change.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تھمانا} (thamānā)}{تھمانا (thamānā)}]{\ur{تھمانا} (thamānā) — to hand (to someone)}

\label{lesson:UR-C425-thamana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for money still owed, then the Urdu for loose change.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تھمانا}}
\textbf{\ur{تھمانا}} — \emph{thamānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to hand (to someone)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دکاندار} \ur{نے} \ur{مجھے} \ur{تھیلا} \ur{تھمایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dukāndār ne mujhe thailā thamāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper handed me the bag.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{چابی} \ur{تھمائی}, \emph{us ne chābī thamāī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تھمانا}} (\emph{thamānā}) is built on \emph{thāmnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to hold, to prop\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under Sanskrit \emph{stambhate}, \textquotedblleft{}props, stops\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13683): this is the form for making someone hold a thing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{thamānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{thamānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dukāndār ne mujhe thailā thamāyā.} — The shopkeeper handed me the bag.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for money still owed, then the Urdu for loose change, then say \emph{thamānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{تھمانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To hand (to someone)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Accounts and Instalments to Scales and Change}

\label{lesson:UR-R425-review-418-425}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for a reckoning and interest (on money).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a reckoning, interest (on money), an instalment, a payment, to bring down (a price)
  \item a profit, a business loss, capital (money), an asset, to pack up
  \item an income, a budget, thrift, to share out, to cash (a cheque)
  \item paper, a card, a token, a fee, a currency
  \item a broker, property, insurance, to collect (money owed), to give back
  \item a deal, the going rate, the asking price, a discount, a sale (at low prices)
  \item goods (for sale), a stockpile, a sack, a packet, to wrap
  \item a pair of scales, free of charge, money still owed, loose change, to hand (to someone)
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A reckoning? (\textbf{\ur{حساب}}, \emph{hisāb}.) Interest (on money)? (\textbf{\ur{سود}}, \emph{sūd}.) An instalment? (\textbf{\ur{قسط}}, \emph{qist}.) A payment? (\textbf{\ur{ادائیگی}}, \emph{adāigī}.) To bring down (a price)? (\textbf{\ur{گھٹانا}}, \emph{ghaṭānā}.) A profit? (\textbf{\ur{منافع}}, \emph{munāfā}.) A business loss? (\textbf{\ur{خسارہ}}, \emph{khasārā}.) Capital (money)? (\textbf{\ur{سرمایہ}}, \emph{sarmāyā}.) An asset? (\textbf{\ur{اثاثہ}}, \emph{asāsā}.) To pack up? (\textbf{\ur{سمیٹنا}}, \emph{sameṭnā}.) An income? (\textbf{\ur{آمدنی}}, \emph{āmdanī}.) A budget? (\textbf{\ur{بجٹ}}, \emph{bajaṭ}.) Thrift? (\textbf{\ur{کفایت}}, \emph{kifāyat}.) To share out? (\textbf{\ur{بانٹنا}}, \emph{bāṅṭnā}.) To cash (a cheque)? (\textbf{\ur{بھنانا}}, \emph{bhunānā}.) Paper? (\textbf{\ur{کاغذ}}, \emph{kāghaz}.) A card? (\textbf{\ur{کارڈ}}, \emph{kārḍ}.) A token? (\textbf{\ur{ٹوکن}}, \emph{ṭokan}.) A fee? (\textbf{\ur{فیس}}, \emph{fīs}.) A currency? (\textbf{\ur{کرنسی}}, \emph{karansī}.) A broker? (\textbf{\ur{دلال}}, \emph{dallāl}.) Property? (\textbf{\ur{جائیداد}}, \emph{jāidād}.) Insurance? (\textbf{\ur{بیمہ}}, \emph{bīmā}.) To collect (money owed)? (\textbf{\ur{وصول} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{vusūl karnā}.) To give back? (\textbf{\ur{لوٹانا}}, \emph{lauṭānā}.) A deal? (\textbf{\ur{سودا}}, \emph{saudā}.) The going rate? (\textbf{\ur{بھاؤ}}, \emph{bhāo}.) The asking price? (\textbf{\ur{دام}}, \emph{dām}.) A discount? (\textbf{\ur{رعایت}}, \emph{riāyat}.) A sale (at low prices)? (\textbf{\ur{سیل}}, \emph{sel}.) Goods (for sale)? (\textbf{\ur{مال}}, \emph{māl}.) A stockpile? (\textbf{\ur{ذخیرہ}}, \emph{zakhīrā}.) A sack? (\textbf{\ur{بوری}}, \emph{borī}.) A packet? (\textbf{\ur{پیکٹ}}, \emph{paikaṭ}.) To wrap? (\textbf{\ur{لپیٹنا}}, \emph{lapeṭnā}.) A pair of scales? (\textbf{\ur{ترازو}}, \emph{tarāzū}.) Free of charge? (\textbf{\ur{مفت}}, \emph{muft}.) Money still owed? (\textbf{\ur{بقایا}}, \emph{baqāyā}.) Loose change? (\textbf{\ur{ریزگاری}}, \emph{rezgārī}.) To hand (to someone)? (\textbf{\ur{تھمانا}}, \emph{thamānā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
